replies.author: Jihaijoh
replies.body:
I would. It doesn’t mean it’s right. And I understand how it can be received. Being mean to you wasn’t my intention. I am sorry if it came out that way. 

I think both « parts » of what I said. I think one can see you poured work in this game. And that you have a dream and objective. I also hate how AI pillages everything it can reach and how nothing, truly nothing, is sacred anymore.

But the issue is, as always, more complex and nuanced than that. Putting a team together is hard, defining what’s sacred/art or what’s not even more. I speak to devs daily who are losing all hope in the future, and all drive to learn anything new. I see artists putting their work out here on Reddit and see their idea copied and regurgitated 300 times in the following days. I also see people enabled, who always dreamed to do this game or carried this idea in them for years but didn’t get the opportunity, means or grit to do it.

I’m not here to fight. For real. I reacted poorly and ask you to forgive me. We are collectively killing the Deer God. But the Deer God is us in the end. Our ability to create and find beauty, connexion, meaning. I feel we are all kinda lost nowadays. This era sucks and the issues we face go far beyond game dev with or without AI. 

So I should have been more considerate.

To answer your question in a more practical manner I think you have two directions :

\- Go to the end of this project. Ship it. And see what you learn. The experience you’ll acquire going through the whole process will be valuable. You won’t avoid the hate coming with picking this exact art style, but in the end you wouldn’t be the first, and it’s valuable data too. 

\- Consider you were only half way and try to look for reskinning the game. Either associate with an artist (a complex but interesting endeavour) or try to find ways to develop something unique with the skills youve acquired. 

I would only consider the second option if the game is actually fun and you see a real potential in it. You could also stash it, start anew or release it for free with a more « fan project context ». I dont know you, your situation nor what the best course of action would be for you. 

Do consider, to conclude, that if you’re truly able to ship an interesting project with AI and you did it alone and enjoyed the process then you’re already winning. Most people are currently scrambling to understand how and what to do with this shit. If you figured it out, or some part of it, you have figured out something valuable. 

As I said, I wish you the best, truly. Even if I am at odds with some aspects of the result, I don’t wish you to fail.

replies.author: DrinkTeaFightMonster
replies.body:
You create the still image first, make sure it fits on the battle background.

Then you decide which animations you want for enemies e.g. idle, hit-reaction, attack, death. 

You create each of them on Kling through a prompt. Animation AI is even more finicky than LLMs, you will likely need to rewrite your prompts many times. 

Later on as it gets more complex, you will need to do more complicated things to make the animation work. For example, you want an animation of it roaring and you're struggling with the KlingAI generation. What you need to do is take the base image, and ask your image generation AI to create another still of the enemy at the apex of its roar. Then on KlingAI, you put the start frame of the animation as the idle and the apex roar as the end frame of the animation, and you tell it to animate from idle to roar. 

Lastly, you will need to work with your LLM (Claude/Codex/whatever) to search through the various KlingAI generations to see if you can stitch together something that works. Like, x frames from animation A, x frames from animation B. Splice them together. 

It's by far the most painful part of the whole equation.

replies.author: DrinkTeaFightMonster
replies.body:
The ideal is of course, the actual current game dev way of using spine animation. 

AI cannot work well with spine today; it generates art holistically and not by parts. So it cannot work with spine in a way you will be satisfied. I tried.

You have to accept that limitation and work with reduced frames, more compression and in my experience, if you use procedural VFX you will move the visual load of the scene away from animation to an overall visual impression. 

We do what we can with today's tech but it is getting better everyday.

replies.author: DrinkTeaFightMonster
replies.body:
I haven't, at first it was just using what I had. Gemini was the first LLM I had a subscription to, and I was using it just for regular stuff -- asking about random things in the world. Why does this road bump have splits in between. Why do some mountains in Banff have red trees and some only green. 

So I used NBP as I had Gemini, and Imagegen from OpenAI wasn't better -- it frequently produced a weird grain in its gen art. 

Never thought of using Midjourney

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body:
Midjourney is by far my favorite hem AI, you have so much artistic control, you can train it on particular styles by feeding it images to a better extent than Gemini and ChatGPT. I'm banned for life though because I ran some bots a couple of years ago and I haven't bothered to work around it.

My experience with Gemini was that it has smoother pixel art styles out of the box than chatgpt, but chatgpt has better composition. What's your thoughts about that though? I haven't used it for about a year

replies.author: DrinkTeaFightMonster
replies.body:
I'm eager to streamline and keep as small a working pipeline as possible to complete the game but based on your words I will try out Midjourney in the future. 

I don't think composition was an issue for me, because the composition comes from the very detailed prompt. So it was more rendering consistency for me and I could never get Codex/Imagegen to consistently render enough art in the same style for me to broadly use it. It did generate a lot of the smaller art like charm icons, and it was good enough in the "on-hit reaction" still that it generated that for the characters for me as well. 

The last big thing is Nano Banana Pro exports 2K and 4K with a $20 subscription, while OpenAI's Imagegen is sub-2k. Going above requires API usage, no matter your subscription.

Thank you. The first character is going to be more standard. Games usually need to open with something more square and understandable. 

I am going to try and push the innovation with the 2nd character, Whistler and her animal companions.

If we get to the 3rd, it's even more boundary pushing. 

I will try my best to deliver something people will like to play!

comments.author: Laicbeias
comments.body:
Its looks amazing but you will generate so much hate. Its like stomping on Ghibli. Like if you choose one style to put a target on your game its that one. 

It was incredible tone deaf and disrespectful from OpenAI to copy that.
Im not saying you shouldnt use it, but buckle in, you are basically using one of the most iconic and loved anime styles there is. Ripping out its soul - in bird language that is going to be considered a dick move. 

Its like screaming idk go back to the kitchen to a feminist event. And the web usually unloads on stuff like that.
Add some idk trump stickers and leftist tears stomp somewhere, with a rainbow flag and pro lgptq+ stuff,  heck and a israel and palestina flag - so it looks like performance art.

comments.author: IamLordeyayaya_0
comments.body: I personally like the art style. You will get ridiculed for it. For obvious reasons. Personally I don't think the style here is 1 to 1 with studio Ghibli's work. So, plagiarism never crossed my mind, inspired by or heavily inspired by. Were my first thoughts. Keep up the good work.. I would totally play this

replies.author: DrinkTeaFightMonster
replies.body:
It's not a 1:1 copy at all, but I can't fight with prospective customers. 

A full art rework is now on the way.

I think Ghibli and its childlike wonder of the movies means it occupies this very pure space in our hearts. In the end we all feel what we all feel. To me, doing it this way showed love. Who would make a game in a vision they hated? 

But obviously it doesn't come across that way, I'm OK with that reality and can steer.

replies.author: IamLordeyayaya_0
replies.body: I agree. Hey, do what you gotta do. But (imo) don't compromise your vision.

comments.author: TimSimpson
comments.body:
First of all, great work overall! I can see the effort you put into this. 

That said, while I personally like the ghibli style (minus a few blatant ripoffs like the wolf), I would encourage you to rework the card frame, as it feels very derivative of Slay the Spire. Otherwise, keep doing what you're doing man! I've wishlisted it on steam, and I'm looking forward to seeing where you take this project!
